text: Make a time series of Euler mathoed and render 3d

Given: Differential equation: dy/dt=-y, Initial condition: y(0)=1, Exact solution: y_exact(t)=e^{-t}, Time interval: 0\le t\le 1, Fixed Euler step size: h=0.1, Grid indices: n=0,1,\ldots,10, 3D axes: time t, numerical value y_n, and absolute error e_n
Find: The Euler numerical trajectory, its pointwise error relative to the exact solution, and the corresponding animated 3D data points.

1. Specify the differential equation and initial condition
   (dy)/(dt)=-y, y(0)=1
   We study the initial-value problem in which the rate of change of y is the negative of its current value. The initial numerical value is 1 at time 0.

2. Find the exact reference solution
   yₑₓₐcₜ(t)=e⁻ᵗ
   Solving the initial-value problem gives the exact solution y(t)=e^{-t}. This solution will be plotted as a reference against the Euler approximation.

3. Choose the time grid and step size
   tₙ=nh, h=0.1, n=0,1,…,10
   Take a fixed step size h=0.1 over the interval from 0 to 1. The grid points are t_0=0, t_1=0.1, and so on, through t_{10}=1.

4. Apply the Euler tangent-line approximation
   yₙ₊₁=yₙ+h f(tₙ,yₙ)=yₙ+h(-yₙ)
   Euler's method replaces the unknown solution over one short time interval by its tangent-line prediction. Since the slope is f(t_n,y_n)=-y_n, the next numerical value is obtained by adding h times this slope.

5. Simplify the update for this particular equation
   yₙ₊₁=yₙ+h(-yₙ)=yₙ(1-h)
   For the chosen equation, the Euler update is a multiplication by 1-h. The algebraic identity z+h(-z)=z(1-h) has been symbolically verified.

6. Compute the first Euler step explicitly
   y₁=y₀(1-h)=1(1-0.1)=0.9
   Starting from y_0=1 at t_0=0, the first Euler step gives y_1=0.9 at t_1=0.1.

7. Generate the complete numerical trajectory
   y₀=1, y₁=0.9, y₂=0.81, y₃=0.729, …, y₁₀=0.3486784401
   Repeatedly applying the update y_{n+1}=0.9y_n produces the numerical time series. The computed trajectory begins 1, 0.9, 0.81, 0.729 and ends at approximately 0.3486784401 when t=1.

8. Define the pointwise numerical error
   eₙ= |yₙ-yₑₓₐcₜ(tₙ) |= |yₙ-e⁻ᵗ_ⁿ |
   At each grid time, compare the Euler value with the exact value at the same time. The absolute difference e_n measures the vertical error of the numerical approximation.

9. Evaluate representative exact values and errors
   e₁= |0.9-e⁻⁰.¹ |≈ 0.0048374180, e₁₀= |0.3486784401-e⁻¹ |≈ 0.0192010011
   At t=0.1, the Euler value is slightly above the exact value, producing an error of about 0.00484. At t=1, the accumulated error is about 0.01920.

10. Construct the three-dimensional data points
   Pₙ=bigl (tₙ, yₙ, eₙbigr )= (tₙ, yₙ, |yₙ-e⁻ᵗ_ⁿ | )
   Represent every Euler sample by a 3D point. The first coordinate is time, the second is the numerical solution value, and the third is the corresponding absolute error.

11. Add the exact solution to the 3D visualization
   Cₑₓₐcₜ(t)=bigl (t, e⁻ᵗ, 0bigr ), 0le tle 1
   The exact solution is plotted as a continuous curve in the plane where the error coordinate is zero. This makes the exact trajectory a reference path while the Euler points show both approximation and error.

12. Animate one Euler step at a time
   Pₙlongrightarrow Pₙ₊₁, n=0,1,…,9
   At animation frame n, display the points and line segments through P_0 up to P_n. Then compute and reveal P_{n+1}, showing the forward time step, the updated numerical value, and the newly accumulated error.

13. Interpret the three-dimensional geometry
   time=tₙ, numerical value=yₙ, error=eₙ
   Motion along the time axis shows forward integration. The second coordinate shows the decay of the numerical solution, while the third coordinate shows how far the Euler approximation is from the exact solution at each time.

14. State the complete visualization formula
   boxed Pₙ= (nh, yₙ, |yₙ-e⁻ⁿʰ | ), y₀=1, yₙ₊₁=yₙ(1-h), h=0.1, n=0,…,10
   This boxed expression is the final construction for the 3D Euler time series. Generate y_n recursively, place each value at time nh, compute its absolute error against e^{-nh}, and animate the points in increasing n. Plot the exact comparison curve as (t,e^{-t},0).

Answer: boxed Pₙ= (nh, yₙ, |yₙ-e⁻ⁿʰ | ), y₀=1, yₙ₊₁=yₙ(1-h), h=0.1, n=0,…,10
Use Euler's method with h=0.1 to generate y_0=1 and y_{n+1}=0.9y_n. For each n, plot the 3D point P_n=(t_n,y_n,e_n)=(nh,y_n,|y_n-e^{-nh}|). Reveal these points sequentially to animate the numerical integration. Plot the exact reference curve as (t,e^{-t},0) for 0\le t\le 1.

14 steps, 15 slides — 3 step(s) sympy could not prove — 53% of slides draw a figure Illustrated 5 slide(s).

operations.title: The decay problem
operations.caption: \frac{dy}{dt}=-y,\qquad y(0)=1
operations.narration: We begin with a quantity whose rate of change is the negative of its current value, starting from one at time zero.

operations.title: The exact path
operations.caption: y_{\mathrm{exact}}(t)=e^{-t}
operations.narration: The exact solution is the smooth exponential decay curve, e to the negative t.

operations.title: A ten-step grid
operations.caption: t_n=nh,\qquad h=0.1,\qquad n=0,1,\ldots,10
operations.narration: Instead of following the curve continuously, we sample time in ten equal steps of length zero point one.

operations.title: Follow the tangent
operations.caption: y_{n+1}=y_n+h\,f(t_n,y_n)=y_n+h(-y_n)
operations.narration: At each known point, Euler follows the tangent for one short time step. The slope is the differential equation evaluated at the current point.

operations.title: The update rule
operations.caption: y_{n+1}=y_n+h(-y_n)=y_n(1-h)
operations.narration: For this particular equation, adding the negative slope is the same as multiplying by one minus the step size.

operations.title: The first step
operations.caption: y_1=y_0(1-h)=1(1-0.1)=0.9
operations.narration: Starting from one, the first Euler step moves forward by zero point one and gives a new value of zero point nine.

operations.title: The numerical trajectory
operations.caption: y_0=1,\quad y_1=0.9,\quad y_2=0.81,\quad y_3=0.729,\quad \ldots,\quad y_{10}=0.3486784401
operations.narration: Repeating the same multiplication produces the Euler time series, ending at about zero point three four eight seven at time one.

operations.title: Measure the gap
operations.caption: e_n=\left|y_n-y_{\mathrm{exact}}(t_n)\right|=\left|y_n-e^{-t_n}\right|
operations.narration: At every time grid point, the error is the vertical distance between the Euler value and the exact value.

operations.title: Error accumulates
operations.caption: e_1=\left|0.9-e^{-0.1}\right|\approx0.0048374180,\qquad e_{10}=\left|0.3486784401-e^{-1}\right|\approx0.0192010011
operations.narration: After the first step the error is about zero point zero zero four eight four. By time one, it has grown to about zero point zero one nine two.

operations.title: Make error a dimension
operations.caption: P_n=\bigl(t_n,y_n,e_n\bigr)=\left(t_n,y_n,\left|y_n-e^{-t_n}\right|\right)
operations.narration: Each sample now becomes a point whose coordinates are time, numerical value, and error.

operations.title: The exact reference curve
operations.caption: C_{\mathrm{exact}}(t)=\bigl(t,e^{-t},0\bigr),\qquad 0\le t\le1
operations.narration: The exact solution lies in the zero-error plane and provides a continuous reference path for the Euler points.

operations.title: Step through time
operations.caption: P_n\longrightarrow P_{n+1},\qquad n=0,1,\ldots,9
operations.narration: Reveal the numerical trajectory one step at a time. Each point advances in time, decays in value, and rises according to its accumulated error.

operations.title: Read the 3D picture
operations.caption: \text{time}=t_n,\qquad \text{numerical value}=y_n,\qquad \text{error}=e_n
operations.narration: Time moves forward, the Euler value decays, and the third coordinate records the distance from the exact solution.

operations.title: The complete construction
operations.caption: \boxed{P_n=\left(nh,\,y_n,\,\left|y_n-e^{-nh}\right|\right),\quad y_0=1,\quad y_{n+1}=y_n(1-h),\quad h=0.1,\quad n=0,\ldots,10}
operations.narration: The construction is complete: generate the Euler values recursively, attach their absolute errors, and place the points at their corresponding times.

operations.title: FINAL ANSWER
operations.caption: \boxed{P_n=\left(nh,\,y_n,\,\left|y_n-e^{-nh}\right|\right),\quad y_0=1,\quad y_{n+1}=y_n(1-h),\quad h=0.1,\quad n=0,\ldots,10}
operations.narration: Using step size zero point one, repeatedly apply y sub n plus one equals zero point nine y sub n. Each point records time, numerical value, and absolute error from the exact exponential solution.
